payload.scores:
Scored 1-5 against the nine criteria. Vetoes are pass/fail, not scores. Weighted total counts only C3-C9.

                                 wt   X1 fit-per-job   X2 one-searcher   X3 fit + meaning
C1 freshness            VETO      —   PASS            FAIL              PASS
C2 reach                VETO      —   PASS            PASS              PASS
C3 one-click install      5           4               5                 4
C4 structured output      4           5               3                 5
C5 one impl per job       5           5               5                 5
C6 bounded cost           3           4               4                 4
C7 selection correctness  5           5               5                 2
C8 no migration debt      2           3               3                 5
C9 own-failure evidence   5           5               2                 3
WEIGHTED TOTAL (C3-C9)          —   136             117               113

THE SCORES THAT DECIDE, with their reasons — the rest are close enough not to matter.

C1 FRESHNESS, and X2 FAILS THE VETO. This is the finding of the state and it was not visible before the chart separated the two rows. Version-control grep searches TRACKED CONTENT. A file the agent created seconds ago and has not staged is invisible to it — not slow, not partial: absent, reported as 'no match'. The agent's dominant pattern is reading back what it just wrote, so X2's answer to 'is my new module there' is a confident no. That is precisely C1's definition of a wrong answer wearing a confident face. X2 does not lose on points; it is disqualified.
  Recorded honestly: the first pass CHOSE X2 and never noticed this, because it never asked the freshness question separately of the two rows. The veto existed and was not applied.

C4 STRUCTURED OUTPUT. X1 and X3 score 5 — the packaged searcher emits typed records with line numbers, spans and submatches. X2 scores 3: version-control grep emits delimited text that must be parsed, and its output shape shifts between the working-tree and ref cases, which is exactly where a parser silently mis-reads an edge case.

C5 ONE IMPLEMENTATION PER JOB. All three score 5 under the CORRECTED definition, and that is the point: C5 stopped being a discriminator the moment the job boundary was drawn correctly. Every candidate deletes the hand-rolled scanner; none keeps two paths for one question. Under the first pass's mis-definition this criterion produced the whole wrong answer by itself. A criterion that decides everything is usually a criterion that has been misdefined.

C7 SELECTION CORRECTNESS. X1 and X3 differ only here, and it is decisive between them. X1 scores 5: declared applicability is checkable — a rule either names this state or it does not, and F29 reports the rules that name nothing. X3 scores 2: semantic matching cannot be checked without a ground truth we do not have, and its failure mode is the worst available — plausible-but-wrong rules delivered confidently, costing attention while looking like coverage. C7 is weight 5 for exactly this.

C8 NO MIGRATION DEBT. X3 wins at 5 (nothing to migrate) against 3 for the others (ten nodes plus authoring going forward). Weight 2 deliberately, so this cannot buy C7 back — and the low weight was set BEFORE the scores, not after.

C9 EVIDENCE FROM OUR OWN FAILURES. X1 scores 5: it is the design that today's measurements point at — P1 (the searcher is not on the PATH, so the package IS the delivery), P2 (ref search works and parses), P3 (the ref ambiguity is real), and the four-calls-per-answer cost recorded in R3. X2 scores 2: it contradicts a measured local failure without naming a difference — the first pass adopted it and the owner's correction, plus the untracked-file veto, are both against it. X3 scores 3: neutral on search, unmeasured on selection, and C9 explicitly scores absence of evidence as neutral rather than as a mark against.

STRUCTURE METRICS over the allocated elements, same relation meaning as the DSM.
  X1: 9 elements, 14 inter-element edges, longest dependency chain 4. Retrieval splits into a working-tree element and a record element that share ONE addressing contract — the highest-coupling seam in the design, and it is a contract seam rather than a data seam, which is the kind that stays stable.
  X2: 8 elements, 12 edges, chain 4. Genuinely simpler, and its simplicity is real rather than nominal. Its cost is the veto.
  X3: 9 elements, 15 edges, chain 5 — selection-by-meaning adds a scoring stage between rule storage and packet assembly.
  All three keep K4 and K5 adjacent, so none is scored down on the partitioning's strong claim. All three keep F33 and F34 in ONE element, per the second strong claim; a fourth combination that split them was not enumerated, because the chart records the re-arm as inseparable rather than optional.

THE FORMULATED EXAMPLES, WALKED THROUGH EACH CANDIDATE — this is what turned the veto from an argument into an observation.
  UC-B step 3 'find a fact and read the lines around it': X1 one call with context. X2 one call, context available, BUT the agent's own newly written file is invisible. X3 as X1.
  UC-B ext 2a 'find what a shipped iteration decided': identical in all three — all use ref search, which is why Row 2 has one surviving option.
  UC-H 'the law minted this afternoon reaches the packet': X1 and X2 deliver it if the rule declares applicability, and REPORT it if it declares none. X3 delivers whatever scores highest, and neither the agent nor the owner can tell a correct selection from a plausible one.
  UC-A ext 6a 'the reopen re-activates and leaves the gate reachable': identical in all three.
  UC-D 'promote an engine change': identical in all three.
  THE WALK'S OWN FINDING: three of the five examples do not discriminate at all. That is a good sign about the chart — the rows with one surviving option really did have one — and it concentrates the whole decision onto two questions: can the searcher see an unstaged file, and is rule selection checkable.
payload.front:
THE NON-DOMINATED SET: {X1}. A front of one, which is unusual enough to state plainly rather than present as a tidy result.

X1 dominates X3 outright — it is better or equal on every criterion except C8 (weight 2), and worse there by 2 points against a 15-point advantage on C7. There is no weighting of the declared criteria under which X3 wins, and I checked that rather than assuming it: X3 would need C8 to outweigh C7, which would mean caring more about not rewriting ten nodes than about whether the rules delivered are the right ones.
X2 is not on the front at all — it fails a veto, and a veto is not a low score.

WHY A FRONT OF ONE IS HONEST HERE RATHER THAN CONVENIENT. Set-based design expects a front with several survivors, and a single survivor usually means the candidates were not genuinely different. These were: X2 was the FIRST PASS'S OWN CHOICE, carried forward as a real contender and scored on its merits, and it collapsed on a veto that the first pass had written down and never applied. X3 is genuinely attractive on cost and dies on a quality that cannot be measured without a spike. The space narrowed because two vetoes and one weight-5 criterion did their job, not because only one option was ever considered.

WHAT STAYS OPEN INSIDE X1, so the front is not falsely tidy: X1 fixes that rules are selected by DECLARED applicability, but not the selector's vocabulary — state ids, state kinds, or tags. That is a live choice inside the surviving candidate, and it goes to the spike alongside the migration of the ten existing nodes.
payload.eliminations:
X2 ONE-SEARCHER — ELIMINATED ON THE C1 FRESHNESS VETO.
Reason, stated as an observation rather than a preference: version-control grep searches tracked content, so a file the agent wrote seconds ago and has not staged is invisible to it, and the search reports no match rather than reporting that it could not see. The agent's dominant working pattern is reading back what it just wrote. C1 is a veto precisely because a stale or blind source is not a worse answer but a confident wrong one.
WHAT IT WAS BETTER AT, said first because a comparison that only lists the loser's faults is not a comparison: X2 is the simplest design here. One search mechanism, one code path, one fewer dependency, eight elements instead of nine, and no exposure to a package failing to resolve a binary. It scores 5 on one-click installability against X1's 4. If the working tree could be searched by version control without the blind spot, X2 would win.
WHAT THIS ELIMINATION COST US ALREADY: X2 was adopted by the first pass and the veto was not applied to it. The owner caught the error from the outside — 'this is not one job, it's two jobs' — before the scoring did. That is the single most important line in this state, and it is recorded here rather than in a retro note, because the elimination is only trustworthy if the reason it was missed the first time is visible beside it.

X3 FIT-PER-JOB WITH RULES BY MEANING — ELIMINATED AS DOMINATED, on C7 selection correctness.
Reason: semantic selection cannot be checked. A rule that scores highly against a state's statement may still be the wrong rule, and there is no ground truth here to tell the difference. Its failure mode is the one the risk register already names — the join buries the instruction — with the added property that a wrong selection is indistinguishable from a right one.
WHAT IT WAS BETTER AT: migration cost, decisively. X3 needs nothing rewritten and nothing authored going forward, which also means it works on rules written by someone who never heard of the selector. That is a real advantage for a method meant to be used by people who did not build it.
NOT DISCARDED, DEFERRED: X3's mechanism is the natural fallback if declared applicability proves too burdensome to author in practice, and the spike that measures X1's selector vocabulary should record what X3 would have selected for the same states. That comparison is nearly free at spike time and impossible to reconstruct later.

NOT ELIMINATED, NEVER ENUMERATED, and recorded so the omission is deliberate: a combination splitting F33 (return work) from F34 (keep the path back open) across elements. It is excluded by the chart rather than scored, because this project has already run that configuration by accident and it deadlocked the machine silently. C9 is weight 5 to keep exactly that out of the space.
